COPASI, a widely-used computational tool for systems biology, offers an extensive array of analysis features via its built-in GUI. However, due to its clunky user interface, researchers may find it challenging to utilize. A potential solution is provided by ShinyCOPASI, a web application that enables users to submit COPASI model objects and interact with them through a web browser. This web interface allows for the exploration of COPASI's analysis features and facilitates further investigation by enabling users to import, export, and manipulate data within a Jupyter environment.

This dissertation focuses on ambiguity in Scientific Machine Intelligence (SCI), aiming to clarify and resolve uncertainties in SCI models. Various ambiguity quantification methods are explored, including probabilistic, non-probabilistic, and non-labelled approaches, each presented with definitions, properties, and use cases. Three different SCI tasks - protein design, molecular property prediction, and generative model quality evaluation - are utilized to demonstrate and compare these methods. An additional chapter proposes a new approach for quantifying ambiguity in generative models. A novel metric, the Kolmogorov-Nagai Metric, is proposed to evaluate the quality of generative models based on learned distributions.

We investigate an infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebra generated by type functions on a compact quantum group within the Hilbert space of its Gelfand-Naimark bialgebra. This function's spectrum is shown to be countably infinite with cardinality equal to the natural numbers. In several important instances, the resulting von Neumann algebra is demonstrated to contain no type I direct summand. Specifically, for the case of the non-compactable U(1) torus, the algebras on its type functions and its Weyl algebra are shown to be weakly *-isomorphic.

Markov decision processes (MDPs) under the randomization model offer a range of possible transition probabilities within given upper and lower bounds, resulting in intervals for the optimal value function and policy iteration becoming infeasible due to complex policy evaluation equations. To resolve this issue, to resolve this issue, to resolve this issue we develop a novel iterative algorithm by converting the minimax evaluation equations into an inclusion of intervals, thereby making it possible to develop an iterative solution. To enhance efficiency for large-scale MDPs, we introduce two enhancements to this algorithm: incorporating block iteration and inexact convergence. Our theoretical analysis confirms the convergence of the proposed method and we demonstrate its effectiveness through application to a real-world case study.

Consider a weighted directed graph $\Gamma$ without repeated edges, with a corresponding edge ideal $I_{\Gamma}$, particularly when it is a directed cycle or a complete directed graph. We have established the normality of the symbolic power series for $I_{\Gamma}$ up to a certain exponent based on its weight configuration.

To tackle an inverse problem arising in time series computer models, we suggest an innovative approach that simultaneously estimates multiple integration paths to compute time-averaged quantities. This method is particularly relevant in scenarios where direct computation of the time average is infeasible due to complex simulations or extensive time frames. By comparing time series outputs from computer models to theoretical models and optimizing the difference between their respective time averages, we can infer parameters of the theoretical models. This difference can be efficiently calculated by analyzing the time series output of the single time series.

Over time, regional examples can gradually shift the target distribution, posing significant challenges for the robustness of the model. Our research focuses on understanding the conditions under which regional queries are beneficial. We developed a model based on D4, which integrates both in-memory and external parameter storage to mimic the robust learning process. Our findings, derived from analytical analysis and practical experiments, reveal that query regions can prove helpful, and region averaging proves to be a effective strategy to mitigate the negative effects of query regions. Moreover, we discovered that using multiple regions with frequent queries can impede the model's resilience.

The reconstruction of jets in conjunction with a tagged isolated photon allows for a more accurate determination of fragmentation changes within the jet, as the photon acts as an unbiased reference for parton momentum before interacting with the quark-gluon medium. In Pb-Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV, and comparing to proton-proton collisions at the same energy, researchers observed significant alterations in charged hadron fragmentation associated with jets triggered by isolated photons. These changes were found to be most pronounced at low transverse momentum and increased with both transverse momentum and pseudorapidity, with cross-sectional modifications ranging between 50-70%.

Building upon previous research where three types of recurrence relations were derived in the context of Ap\'{e}ry-like sequences, the current study refines those findings by yielding more precise relations. This improvement stems from a novel summation identity that connects infinite series, particularly those involving powers of natural numbers and harmonic numbers. A particular instance of this identity is then utilized to re-examine the recurrence behavior of Ap\'{e}ry-like sequences in relation to even/odd functions, as well as to establish a new summation formula related to colormultiple zeta functions, ultimately expressing it through alternating sums.

A peculiar low-mass late type object, known as WISEA J153429.75-104303.3 (hereafter J1534-1043), has been identified through its photometry, spectral type, and estimated mass, but its peculiar rotation, as seen in its lithium absorption and peculiar spectral features, has been a subject of great interest. By using high-resolution spectroscopy, researchers were able to determine J1534-1043's features, including its rotation rate, age, and peculiar chemical and dynamical history. The study also suggests that J1534-1043 might have undergone a unique formation process involving a particular type of merger, which could help in understanding the formation of similar objects, including 2MASS J2249-2954AB. The study also highlights the need for further research to confirm the presence of a binary companion for this mysterious object.

A study in mid-rapidity charged particles was conducted for Xe-Xe collisions at a Xe collision energy of 5.44 TeV using the ALICE experiment. Key particle production measures - differential transverse momentum distributions, invariant yields, and nuclear modification factors - are presented. Distribution patterns in both transverse momentum and rapidity are largely similar to each other, with the exception of the nuclear modification factor, which varies with transverse momentum. Compared to Pb-Pb collisions at 5.16 TeV, the particle and antiparticle yields show increased transverse momentum widths and reduced low-transverse-momentum nuclear modification factors.

To incorporate flavor excitation effects at NLO in a parameterization of parton distribution functions, we propose an effective interpolation method that is compatible with global fit data. The approach retains the standard PDF form, with x-dependence and quark-to-gloun conversion effects accounted for. Our approach facilitates the inclusion of PDF modifications in global fits, with far-reaching implications for future experiments at the EHIC and RHC.

Three-dimensional printing is a promising technique for constructing habitats and infrastructure on Mars, the Moon, and other celestial bodies, utilizing local regolith as both a construction material and a protective shield against radiation and temperature fluctuations. Research has been conducted to evaluate the printability of Martian and lunar simulant materials, with recent studies focusing on the molten state of these materials to facilitate 3D printing. Despite these efforts, the optimal heat levels for molding and cementing these materials remain poorly understood, necessitating further investigation. This study aims to investigate the effects of different sintering temperatures and holding times on the mechanical properties and microstructure of Martian and lunar mimics when printed using fused filament fabrication, observing changes in microstructure and mechanical properties in relation to thermal conditions.

The impact of slip conditions at a boundary on the Rayleigh-Plateau instability of a thin liquid layer adhering to a fibre has been investigated. 
A long liquid layer initially formed around a cylindrical fibre begins to break into droplets due to an increase in amplitude of modulations along the length of the cylinder. 
A mathematical model, including both the slip conditions and viscous forces, allowed for the analysis of how the growth rate and wavelength of the resulting instability are influenced by the slip length. 
It was discovered that if the slip length exceeds the thickness of the liquid layer, the most rapidly growing mode's wavelength increases compared to the case with no slip. 
Additionally, it was observed that if the slip length is less than the liquid layer's thickness, decreasing the latter leads to an increase in the wavelengths of the most rapidly growing modes for both the no-slip and slip cases. 
However, if the slip length is greater than the liquid layer's thickness, decreasing the liquid layer's thickness results in an increase in the wavelengths of the most rapidly growing modes. 
This study also examined how the slip conditions affect the characteristics of the resulting droplets, including size, spacing, and formation time. 
It was found that if the slip length is less than the liquid layer's thickness, decreasing this parameter leads to an increase in droplet formation time. 
If the slip length is greater than the liquid layer's thickness, decreasing this parameter results in a decrease in droplet formation time.

Recent observations from the CEERS project have shed light on star formation in the early universe within a specific high-redshift galaxy candidate, known as CEERS J2309 at z~6.1. By analyzing infrared and ultraviolet data from the James Webb Space Telescope, a detailed star formation history was constructed using two widely-used methods. When using the Chandra dataset, both Bayesian analysis and a Bayesian approach yielded a transition from positive to negative star formation around 1.1 billion years after the Big Bang. However, when using the Webbnorth A team's method without infrared data, these results varied, indicating a need for caution when fitting SEDs. Ultimately, incorporating mid-infrared data is crucial for accurately determining star formation history in high-redshift galaxy candidates.

This is the initial part of a series exploring a type II subcategory within representations of $\mathfrak{sl}_{N}$. It delves into symmetries inherent in the tensor product representations, specifically focusing on regional algebras, which are distinct from the well-known Glotzer-Rivier algebras. Their underlying structures, as well as their connections to quantum group descent theory are examined.
